paragraphs.text: People keep proposing what a relation between things could be, and each proposal gets refused. Is it waiting around for each other? No — waiting secretly needs a mind to do the waiting. Is it sitting in two places at once? No — that describes where things are, not what links them. Is it just never being interrupted? No — two iron bars side by side are uninterrupted and unrelated.

What survives is this: the many things share one fused form — many-ness with one selfhood. And the fun part: the Buddhists own proof-verse, which said unmixed things are only joined by thought, gets turned against them — because that joining cannot be pushed away or argued out of happening, which means it is real shining sticking to things, and it can be properly stated on the path of recognition.

What stands: form-fusion, the manys one-selfhood. And the opponents proof-text testifies against itself — unmixed things thought-joined turns out to be unwardable shining-clinging, warrantable inside recognition. Their own verse convicts them.
